thread.title: 5 5G Stocks to Buy That Will Stream Higher Profits for Investors

author: InvestorPlace
title: 5 5G Stocks to Buy That Will Stream Higher Profits for Investors

organizations.name: stock advice & trading tips 7 great vanguard

text:
As telcos launch the first of the 5G networks, 5G stocks will become a focus. The technology will change wireless. How much speed it will add has become a point of controversy. Estimates from a few years ago predicted the improvement at 1,000 times 4G.
More recent estimates peg the improvement at 10 to 20 times 4G LTE. Whatever happens after launch, consumers should see a quantum leap in speed and reliability.
Such speeds will lead to capabilities not possible today. For this reason, it becomes difficult to know whether the innovation will come from one of the large companies or from the mind of an unknown inventor working in his garage.

7 Great Vanguard Funds to Buy Whatever happens, these 5G stocks to buy will likely lead the way in the new networks from a larger company perspective, profiting from 5G while trading at reasonable valuations:
5G Stocks to Buy: Apple (AAPL) 5G Stocks to Buy: Apple (AAPL) More Source: Shutterstock
Although the latest version of the iPhone did not offer 5G capabilities, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) will become one of the more prominent 5G stocks in future years. As one of the primary innovators in the wireless market, Apple will likely continue to enjoy a substantial presence in this industry.
As of the time of this writing, only Apple supports a market cap above $1 trillion. At this size, the laws of mathematics will preclude another 100 fold increase in the stock like it enjoyed over the last 14 years. However, if one’s goals focus on staying rich, Apple could serve that purpose well.
Warren Buffett has made Apple the largest holding in the Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A , NYSE: BRK.B ) portfolio for a reason. AAPL stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 17. Analysts project the company will see 27.7% profit growth this year and an average of 13% growth per year over the next five years.
Also, the stock shows a solid record on dividends . The current yield of 1.3% may not inspire investors. Still, the company has increased its dividend every year since it began paying dividends in 2012. If one keeps AAPL stock as a long-term holding, this dividend will probably become more important.
Apple has not yet released a 5G iPhone. However, as soon as it enters the market, the iPhone will become a critical device for 5G service, and AAPL will become one of the more important 5G stocks. Its investors should benefit.
5G Stocks to Buy: AT&T (T) 5G Stocks to Buy: AT&T (T) More Source: Shutterstock
AT&T (NYSE: T ) will become only one of three companies (assuming T-Mobile (NASDAQ: TMUS ) and Sprint (NYSE: S ) merge) to offer 5G wireless service. This factor in itself makes AT&T one of the more important 5G stocks. Because of the tens of billions of dollars needed to build such a network, the company will probably not have to deal with additional competitors.
The company has struggled recently. Cord-cutting in the pay-TV business, a highly competitive wireless industry and the costly 5G upgrade have weighed on the company. However, this offers a tremendous advantage to those who want to invest now. The recent struggles of the stock have taken its forward P/E to about 9.6. This comes to just over half of the five-year average P/E of 18.6.
Still, the biggest reason to invest lies in the dividend. Its $2 per share annual dividend comes to a yield of just over 5.9%, more than triple the S&P 500 average of 1.9%.
Even better, the psychology that drives T stock insures this dividend will increase. The company has increased the dividend in each of the previous 34 years. For this reason, maintaining the price of T stock hinges heavily on these dividend increases. For this reason, I expect the company will announce another dividend hike in December. The increased revenues that will likely come from 5G will also ensure that the company can afford the dividend increases.
